text:
Choose the correct option for the following reactions.


[IMG]
options: 'A' and 'B' are both Markovnikov addition products.
'A' is Markovnikov  product and 'B' is anti-Markovnikov product.
'B' is Markovnikov  and 'A' is anti-Markovnikov product.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The alkene is 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene, $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$.

Oxymercuration–demercuration ($\mathrm{Hg}(\mathrm{OAc}){}_{2}$, $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, then $\mathrm{NaBH}{}_{4}$) adds $\mathrm{H}$ and $\mathrm{OH}$ in the Markovnikov sense through a bridged mercurinium ion; no free carbocation forms, so no methyl shift occurs. A is 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol, $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, the Markovnikov product.

Hydroboration–oxidation ($(\mathrm{BH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$, then $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}/\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}$) puts boron, and finally $\mathrm{OH}$, on the less substituted terminal carbon. B is 3,3-dimethylbutan-1-ol, $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$, the anti-Markovnikov product.


[IMG]

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: Among the following marked proton of which compound shows lowest $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ value?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Each marked proton is an $α$-C–H, so its acidity depends on how well the carbanion left after its removal is stabilised.

(A) and (D): the carbanion is delocalised onto a $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group whose C=O is already in resonance with the lone pair of $-\mathrm{OH}$ (cross-conjugation), so the C=O stabilises the negative charge poorly.

(B): the carbanion of acetone is delocalised onto one ketone C=O only.

(C): the benzylic carbanion of $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$ is delocalised both onto the ketone C=O and into the benzene ring (extended conjugation), so it is the most stable conjugate base.


[IMG]

The marked proton of (C) is therefore the most acidic and has the lowest $\mathrm{p}K_{\mathrm{a}}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift

text:
For the below given cyclic hemiacetal (X), the correct pyranose structure is :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In converting a Fischer projection to a Haworth (pyranose) projection, a group on the right goes below the ring and a group on the left goes above it. C-5 carries the ring oxygen on the right, so X is a D-sugar and its $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$ (C-6) lies above the ring.

In X: C-1 OH on the left, C-2 OH on the left, C-3 OH on the right, C-4 OH on the left.

So in the ring (ring O, C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4, C-5): C-1 OH up, C-2 OH up, C-3 OH down, C-4 OH up and C-5 $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$ up.


[IMG]

Only option (D) has this arrangement; (A) and (C) have the C-2 and C-4 OH groups below the ring, and (B) has the C-4 OH below the ring. In every option the bend between C-5 and the top OH is the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ of the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$ group.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift

text:
The number of paramagnetic species among the following is $___________$.

$\mathrm{B}_{2},\mathrm{Li}_{2},\mathrm{C}_{2},\mathrm{C}_{2}^{-},\mathrm{O}_{2}^{2-},\mathrm{O}_{2}^{+}$ and $\mathrm{He}_{2}^{+}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Those species which have unpaired electrons are called paramagnetic species.

And those species which have no unpaired electrons are called diamagnetic species.

$B_{2}$ has 10 electrons.

Molecular orbital configuration of $B_{2}$ is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }π_{2p_{x}^{1}}=π_{2p_{y}^{1}}$

Here two unpaired electrons present. So it is paramagnetic. 

$O_{2}^{2-}$ has 18 electrons.

Moleculer orbital configuration of $O_{2}^{2-}$ is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}^{\ast }$

Here is no unpaired electron so it is diamagnetic. 

$O_{2}^{+}$ has 15 electrons. 

Moleculer orbital configuration of $O_{2}^{+}$ is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{1}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{0}}^{\ast }$

Here 1 unpaired electron present, so it is paramagnetic.

$C_{2}$ has 12 electrons. 

Moleculer orbital configuration of $C_{2}$

= $σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}$

Here no unpaired electron present, so it is diamagnetic.

$C_{2}^{-}$ has 13 electrons. 

Moleculer orbital configuration of $C_{2}^{-}$ is

 $σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}σ_{2p_{z}^{1}}$

Here 1 unpaired electron present, so it is paramagnetic.

$Li_{2}$ has 6 electrons.

$Li_{2} =$ $σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }$ $σ_{2s^{2}}$

Here no unpaired electron present, so it is diamagnetic.

Configuration of $He_{2}^{+}$ (3 electrons) is = $σ_{1s^{2}}$ $σ_{1s^{1}}^{\ast }$

Here 1 unpaired electron present, so it is paramagnetic.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift

text: The disproportionation of $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{2-}$ in acidic medium resulted in the formation of two manganese compounds $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$. solution.body:
$3\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-2}^{+6}+4\mathrm{H}^{+}\to \mathrm{MnO}_{2}^{+4}+\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}^{+7}$

$\mathrm{Mn}\to 4s^{2}3d^{5}$

$\mathrm{Mn}^{+4}\to 3d^{3}$

text: Total number of relatively more stable isomer(s) possible for octahedral complex $[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{en})_{2}(\mathrm{SCN})_{2}]$ will be $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$ is $d^{9}$, so the octahedral complex undergoes Jahn-Teller elongation along one axis, giving two long, weak axial bonds.

The two monodentate thiocyanate ligands occupy these trans axial positions while the two en chelates span the equatorial plane, so the trans arrangement is the relatively more stable one and the cis forms are less stable.

Thiocyanate is ambidentate (S- or N-bonded), so the trans isomers are trans-$[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}(\mathrm{SCN}){}_{2}]$, trans-$[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}(\mathrm{NCS}){}_{2}]$ and trans-$[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}(\mathrm{SCN})(\mathrm{NCS})]$.

Hence, the answer is 3.

text: On complete combustion of $0.492\mathrm{g}$ of an organic compound containing $\mathrm{C},\mathrm{H}$ and $\mathrm{O}$, $0.7938\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ and $0.4428\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ was produced. The % composition of oxygen in the compound is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$%$ of $\mathrm{H}=\frac{2}{18}\times \frac{\text{wt. of}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}{\text{wt. of organic compound}}\times 100$

$\begin{array}{l} =\dfrac{2}{18}\times \dfrac{0.4428}{0.492}\times 100 \\  \\ =0.11\times 0.9\times 100 \\  \\ =0.099\times 100=9.9 \end{array}$

$%$ of $C=\frac{12}{44}\times \frac{0.7938}{0.492}\times 100$

$\begin{array}{l} =0.27\times 1.61\times 100 \\  \\ =43.47 \end{array}$

$%\text{Oxygen}=100-(43.47+9.9)$

$=100-53.37\simeq 46$
